subject.title: Rescue: add watchdog core service and cron engine

question: Should OpenClaw core sponsor this `rescueWatchdog` cron/service direction once the stale-branch and proof blockers are fixed, or should the work move under the broader recovery design issue instead?
rationale: The patch adds a new core recovery capability with command execution, service restart, and protocol/storage surface area; after mechanical repair, accepting it still requires maintainer intent about core ownership and security posture.

options.title: Repair before direction review
options.body: Require the contributor or a maintainer repair branch to preserve current cron command/protocol/SQLite behavior and add real recovery proof before making the core-product call.

options.title: Sponsor core rescue now
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the core `rescueWatchdog` direction and then review the repaired branch as the implementation path.

options.title: Route to broader recovery design
options.body: Close or pause this branch in favor of the open recovery/watchdog design issue if maintainers want a different runtime-level approach.

recommendation.title: Repair before direction review
recommendation.body: Require the contributor or a maintainer repair branch to preserve current cron command/protocol/SQLite behavior and add real recovery proof before making the core-product call.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision combines security-sensitive local service control with core recovery ownership, and CODEOWNERS routes relevant cron/gateway security surfaces to this team.
